subject: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan
messages: Subject: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan

Emily — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have everything captured:

Summary of your requirements (as discussed)
- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for short completions (<= 128 tokens).
- Streaming: real-time chunking required; target inter-chunk latency <= 50ms for first-to-subsequent token emission.
- Concurrency: sustained 100 persistent simultaneous connections; spiky bursts to 300 for short windows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~2,000 requests/minute across your busiest region.
- Availability/SLAs: 99.9% monthly uptime target; audit logging required for all inference calls.

Immediate asks we need from you to scope the joint benchmark run:
1) Representative prompt set (we discussed sample lines) — small canonical set (+ pain examples) and a larger production set if available.
2) Any redlines to the SLO definitions (e.g., what you count as a streaming emission).
3) Temporary allowlist for our runner IPs or API keys for a joint run.
4) Window availability for a 2-hour joint run next week (we propose two windows; see below).

What we'll provide from Redwood prior to the run:
- Benchmark config + harness (k6 + custom harness) describing measurement definitions and reproducibility knobs.
- A canary run checklist and an evaluation script to compute p50/p95/p99, streaming inter-chunk latency distribution, and token throughput.

Proposed next steps
- Today: you share the prompt samples and any SLO clarifications (Emily/Rajiv).
- By EOD Fri: Dev/Neha share the benchmark-config.yaml and eval-harness README.
- Next Tue/Wed: joint 2-hour run (canary + full sweep).

Attachments: we can accept the prompt file as CSV/JSON — please attach when convenient.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Monica for procurement once we have window confirmed.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details and attaching a small sample of our prompts (aurelia_prompt_samples.csv).

Clarifications / tweaks from our side:
- P95 200ms applies to short-turn completions (<=128 tokens). For long responses (>128 tokens) we’d accept higher median latency but we still expect steady streaming (no more than 60ms inter-chunk).
- Streaming: our UX requires the first chunk to arrive within 250ms and subsequent chunks not to exceed 50–60ms on average. Please call out how you measure the first-chunk vs inter-chunk.
- Concurrency: 100 persistent connections is baseline; we’ll simulate a 5-minute burst to 300 concurrent connections once per hour.
- Throughput: 2k/minute steady, peaking to 6k/minute during flash events.

A couple of constraints on our side:
- All benchmark traffic must come from an allowlisted set of IPs (we’ll provide Rajiv’s team contact for networking).
- We’ll want the run to include both a cold-start scenario (fresh model spin-up) and warm path with cache hits approximated.

Attached: aurelia_prompt_samples.csv (small representative set).

Availability: Tue 24 Feb between 09:00–12:00 PT or Wed 25 Feb 13:00–16:00 PT both work for our SREs.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Hart
Director of Platform Engineering | Aurelia Health
emily.hart@aureliahealth.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan

Emily / team — thanks for the prompt set. I’m pasting our proposed benchmark methodology and measurement definitions so everyone has a single source of truth before the run. I’ve attached a machine-readable 'benchmark-config.yaml' and a short 'eval-harness-readme.md'.

Benchmark definitions (high level)
- Latency: measure from ingestion (HTTP request complete) to first token emitted (first-chunk) and to last token emitted (response completion). Report p50/p95/p99 for both.
- Streaming inter-chunk latency: measure time between consecutive chunk flushes at the server side and at the client-side capture. We provide both server-side and client-side histograms.
- Cold start vs Warm: cold: model process spin-up + weights load counted (single request to an idle worker pool). Warm: worker with loaded weights and primed KV cache. We’ll run both scenarios.
- Concurrency profile: steady-state load (100 concurrent persistent connections) and spike windows (300 concurrent for 5 minutes).
- Throughput: requests per second and tokens per second; report token emission rate distributions.

Reproducibility controls
- Seeded RNG for generation where applicable; prompt variations deterministic mapping when a seed is present.
- Fixed model artifact version and quantization profile documented in config.
- Hardware profile: we will record GPU type, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and card temperatures.

Harness & tooling
- Primary harness: k6 for load shaping + a lightweight Go harness that opens persistent connections and measures streaming latencies per-chunk.
- Storage: all raw traces and histograms uploaded to the shared Drive link and a small summary JSON.
- Scripts: 'compute_slo_metrics.py' to produce p50/p95/p99 and streaming percentile summaries.

Attachments included: benchmark-config.yaml, eval-harness-readme.md

If these definitions look good to you, we’ll prepare the run checklist and can provision temporary API keys and runner IPs for your network team.

—
Dev Patel
Software Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan

Emily — perfect, thanks. Quick operational checklist and next steps from Redwood: 

1) We’ll share the benchmark-config and harness by EOD today (Dev sent them; see attachments).
2) Please confirm which window you prefer: Tue 24 Feb 09:00–11:00 PT (preferred) or Wed 25 Feb 13:00–15:00 PT. We’ll schedule a joint Zoom and a run coordinator on our side.
3) Networking: Rajiv, please share the allowlist/port rules. We will provide runner IPs and the temporary API key.
4) Metrics we will produce and share within 24 hours after the run: p50/p95/p99 for first-chunk and completion, inter-chunk latency histograms, throughput charts, and a short findings memo with any observed regressions.
5) Procurement: Monica will send a short statement of work and services quote once the run is complete and you’re comfortable with the results.

Links: Drive plan + run checklist (shared in related_links). I’ll book the joint slot for Tue 24 09:00–11:00 PT tentatively and send the calendar invite; please accept or propose an alternate.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint validation.

—
Aditya Rao
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark scope, SLOs, and joint run plan

Aditya / team — thanks, we confirm Tue 24 Feb 09:00–11:00 PT for the joint run (Rajiv and I will be on the call). Monica — I’ll loop in our procurement contact (sow and PO conversation).

A few last items before the run:
- Please share the runner IPs by EOD Mon 23 Feb so our network team can allowlist.
- For cold-start measurement, we’d like the ability to trigger a model process recycle from the Redwood side; can you include that in the checklist?
- We have a short internal NDA addendum that needs to be signed before data collection; I’ll send to Monica.

We’ve attached SLO language we will try to adopt (slo-requirements.pdf) — mostly editorial but useful to align definitions.

Regards —
Emily
